## Natural history notes

A medium-sized water scavenger beetle characterized by a smooth oval body, dark brown to black coloration, short clubbed antennae, and flattened legs used for swimming through still or slow water. In Florida, Tropisternus lateralis is part of the freshwater aquatic beetle fauna and is most likely found in ponds, marshes, ditches, canals, sloughs, wet prairies, and vegetated wetland edges. Adults are mostly scavengers or omnivores that feed on detritus, algae, decaying plant material, and small aquatic organisms, while the larvae are more predatory and help move energy through freshwater food webs.
